title: Rule ID < 128 constraint undocumented on public constructors
description:
Multiple public constructors validate rule_id < 128 but this constraint is not documented in the function signatures or doc comments. Callers must discover it by trial and error or reading source.

**Locations:**
- /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/no_ack.rs:53-55 - NoAckSender::new()
- /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/ack_on_error.rs:172-175 - AckOnErrorSender::new()
- /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/wire.rs:156-162 - check_rule() used by Fragment::write_to
- /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/wire.rs:768-770 - Ack::from_bytes

Internal check_rule() at wire.rs:156 correctly implements this, but the public API docs do not mention it.

**What goes wrong:** A caller using rule IDs 128-255 (e.g., reserving high IDs for application-specific rules) will get FragmentError::InvalidRule at runtime with no prior warning. The error message 'invalid rule ID' gives no hint about the valid range.

**Fix:** 
1. Add to all public function docs that take rule_id: rule_id - SCHC rule ID (must be < 128 per RFC 8724)
2. Improve InvalidRule error to include the invalid value: InvalidRule(u8)
close_reason: Added doc comment to Rule.rule_id explaining <128 constraint for standard SCHC
